```{r general-plot-setting}
# Lato font for all plots 
font_add_google("Lato", "lato")
showtext_auto()

# shared look for all plots in the report 
theme_report <- theme_bw(base_size = 12, base_family = "lato") +
  theme(
    plot.title.position = "panel",
    plot.caption.position = "panel",
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 13, hjust = 0.5,
                                 margin = margin(b = 10)),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey40", hjust = 0),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 14, colour = "black", face = "bold"),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 12, margin = margin(t = 8)),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.key = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = NA)
  )
```

```{r prepare-data}

#Select relevant reference-level variables
count_cols <- c("REKENEN_LAGER1F", "REKENEN_1F", "REKENEN_1S",
                "LV_LAGER1F", "LV_1F", "LV_2F")

# value for DUO's "<5" (1-4 pupils): the midpoint
lt5_value <- 2.5

replace_lt5 <- function(x) {
  x <- as.character(x)
  as.numeric(if_else(x == "<5", as.character(lt5_value), x))
}

#Convert columns to numeric, and turn values like <5 to NA
#Clean reference-level counts
ref_levels <- referentieniveaus |>
  mutate(across(all_of(count_cols), replace_lt5)) |> #used to turn <5 into NA, now into 2.5 to prevent false 100$ scores? For small schools, this quite greatly influenced averages for example. 
  group_by(INSTELLINGSCODE) |>
  summarise(
    GEMEENTENAAM = first(GEMEENTENAAM),
    INSTELLINGSNAAM_VESTIGING = first(INSTELLINGSNAAM_VESTIGING),
    across(all_of(count_cols), ~ sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    #total number of students for maths and for reading
    rekenen_n = REKENEN_LAGER1F + REKENEN_1F + REKENEN_1S,
    reading_n = LV_LAGER1F + LV_1F + LV_2F,
    #percentage of students for each level
    math_1F = 100 * (REKENEN_1F + REKENEN_1S) / rekenen_n,
    math_1S = 100 * REKENEN_1S / rekenen_n,
    reading_1F = 100 * (LV_1F + LV_2F) / reading_n,
    reading_2F = 100 * LV_2F / reading_n
    #DUO only count each pupil once, so to get the totals for reaching 1F in both reading and math, you must also count         the pupils that reached 1S and 2F
  ) |>
  filter(rekenen_n > 0, reading_n > 0)
    #filter out schools where no pupils are counted for maths and reading, this might not occur for Amstelveen, but is          necessary for calculating averages.

#calculate Schoolweging
school_weights <- schoolweging |>
  mutate(INSTELLINGSCODE = str_remove(OVT, "\\|.*$")) |>
  group_by(INSTELLINGSCODE) |>
  summarise(schoolweging = weighted.mean(schoolweging, w = aantal_leerlingen),
    .groups = "drop")

#Combine reference-level results with schoolweging
school_data <- left_join(ref_levels, school_weights, by = "INSTELLINGSCODE")

#Amstelveen Gemeente
amstelveen_data <- filter(school_data, GEMEENTENAAM == "Amstelveen")

#Final data
amstelveen_data |>
  select(INSTELLINGSNAAM_VESTIGING, schoolweging,
          math_1F, math_1S, reading_1F, reading_2F)

```

```{r}
#check data, should be roughly 6000 rows
nrow(school_data)

#check schools that have no schoolweging, will be removed later
school_data |>
  summarise(
    no_schoolweging = sum(is.na(schoolweging)),
    min_sw = min(schoolweging, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_sw = max(schoolweging, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

#check all percentages
school_data |>
  select(math_1F, math_1S, reading_1F, reading_2F) |>
  summary()
```

```{r filter-converse}
# all Dutch schools, one row per school per level
final_data <- school_data |>
  filter(!is.na(schoolweging)) |>
  select(INSTELLINGSNAAM_VESTIGING, GEMEENTENAAM, schoolweging,
         rekenen_n, reading_n,
         math_1F, math_1S, reading_1F, reading_2F) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(math_1F, math_1S, reading_1F, reading_2F),
    names_to = "level",
    values_to = "percentage"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    subject = if_else(str_starts(level, "math"), "Maths", "Reading"),
    type = if_else(str_ends(level, "1F"),
                   "Basic level (1F)",
                   "Target level (1S / 2F)"),
    n_students = if_else(subject == "Maths", rekenen_n, reading_n)
  )

#check if filter and conversion was succesful, are school with no schoolweging really filtered out and is nrow(final_data) x 4 times this amount
count(final_data, level, subject, type)
nrow(final_data)
```
```{r benchmark-regression}
# expected % based on school weighting (all Dutch schools, weighted by
# number of pupils) (regression line); for 1F the benchmark is the fixed 85% norm
final_data <- final_data |>
  group_by(level) |>
  mutate(
    expected = predict(lm(percentage ~ schoolweging, weights = n_students)),
    benchmark = if_else(type == "Basic level (1F)", 85, expected),
    diff = percentage - benchmark
  ) |>
  ungroup()

# check
final_data |>
  group_by(level) |>
  summarise(
    mean_diff = weighted.mean(diff, n_students),
    below = sum(diff < 0)
  )
# 2F and 1S should be near zero, it is a weighted (so takes into account number of students) regression line, so runs through weighted middle of the data.  middle
# remember: regression line = average that moves along with the schoolweging
```
Maths norm much harder to reach than reading.

```{r split-data-per-layer}
# grey background: all Dutch schools
# national <- final_data coded out, the grey dots were messy

# the municipality we highlight
municipality <- "Amstelveen"

muni_data <- final_data |>
  filter(GEMEENTENAAM == municipality) |>
  mutate(passed = if_else(percentage >= 85, "Yes", "No"))

# Amstelveen dots, split per row of the plot (each gets its own colours)
muni_1f <- filter(muni_data, type == "Basic level (1F)")
muni_target <- filter(muni_data, type == "Target level (1S / 2F)")
```

```{r names-in-plot}
# names in the 1F plot: only the schools below the 85% norm;
# De Akker gets an asterisk, because whether it meets the norm depends
# on the "<5" choice (robustness check with 1, 2.5 and 4)
label_data <- muni_data |>
  filter(type == "Basic level (1F)", passed == "No") |>
  mutate(label = paste0(
    INSTELLINGSNAAM_VESTIGING,
    if_else(INSTELLINGSNAAM_VESTIGING == "De Akker", "*", ""),
    "\n", round(percentage, 2), "%"
  ))

# schools whose classification at the advanced level depends on the
# "<5" choice (robustness check with 1, 2.5 and 4)
sensitive_target <- c("Elif Amstelveen", "Roelof Venemaschool", "Het Palet")

# school name for the y-axis; an asterisk marks the schools listed above
muni_target <- muni_target |>
  mutate(school_label = paste0(
    INSTELLINGSNAAM_VESTIGING,
    if_else(INSTELLINGSNAAM_VESTIGING %in% sensitive_target, "*", "")
  ))
```

```{r scatter-1f-final, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 7, warning = FALSE}
plot_1f <- ggplot(muni_1f, aes(x = schoolweging, y = percentage)) +
  # the Inspectorate's fixed 85% norm
  geom_hline(yintercept = 85, color = "grey30", linewidth = 1) +
  # dot = meets the norm, cross = below it, colours also
  # work for colour-blind readers
  # green = meets the 85% norm, magenta = below it
  geom_point(aes(color = passed, size = n_students)) +
  # names of the schools below the norm: right of the dot, below the line
  geom_text_repel(data = filter(label_data, type == "Basic level (1F)"),
                  aes(label = label), size = 3.5, lineheight = 0.9,
                  family = "lato",
                  nudge_x = 0.6, nudge_y = -1, hjust = 0, direction = "y",
                  segment.color = NA, seed = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Yes" = "#26AB6F", "No" = "#AB2662"),
                     name = "Meets 85% norm") +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 5, name = "Pupils tested") +
  guides(
    color = guide_legend(order = 1, override.aes = list(size = 4)),
    size = guide_legend(order = 2)
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ subject, labeller = as_labeller(c(
    Maths = "Maths (1F)", Reading = "Reading (1F)"
  ))) +
  labs(
    title = paste(
      "Almost all schools in Amstelveen reach the basic reference",
      "level;\nonly two fall below the national signalling value."
    ),
    subtitle = paste(
      "90% of schools (n = 18) meet the 85% norm in both subjects,",
      "while 10% (n = 2) do not."
    ),
    x = "School weighting (higher = more disadvantaged pupils)",
    y = "% of pupils reaching 1F",
    caption = paste0(
      "Each dot is one Amstelveen primary school (n = 20). Line: the ",
      "Inspectorate's signalling value of 85%, the same for all schools\n",
      "(Staatscourant 2026, nr. 26023). * Classification changes ",
      "depending on how DUO's '<5' counts are handled (tested with 1, 2.5\n",
      "and 4). In this plot '<5' counts are replaced by 2.5. Source: DUO."
    )
  ) +
  theme_report
plot_1f
```

```{r dot-1f-2s-plot, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6}
plot_1s_2f <- ggplot(
  muni_target,
  aes(x = diff, y = reorder(school_label, diff), colour = diff)
) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "black", linetype = "dashed",
             linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(size = n_students)) +
  scale_colour_gradient2(
    low = "#AB2662", mid = "grey85", high = "#26AB6F", midpoint = 0,
    # differences of 10 or more points already get the strongest colour
    limits = c(-10, 10), oob = scales::squish,
    breaks = c(-10, -5, 0, 5, 10),
    labels = c("-10 or less", "-5", "0", "+5", "+10 or more"),
    name = "Difference from\nexpected\n(percentage points)"
  ) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 5, name = "Pupils tested") +
  facet_wrap(~ subject, labeller = as_labeller(c(
    Maths = "Maths (1S)", Reading = "Reading (2F)"
  ))) +
  labs(
    title = paste(
      "Most schools in Amstelveen are on track at the advanced reference",
      "level;\nnine fall behind the expected score in at least one subject."
    ),
    subtitle = paste(
      "55% of schools (n = 11) score at or above expected in both",
      "subjects, while 45% (n = 9) do not."
    ),
    x = "Percentage points above (+) or below (-) expected",
    y = NULL,
    caption = paste0(
      "Dashed line: expected share of pupils reaching the advanced ",
      "reference level for schools with a similar school weighting,\n",
      "based on a regression on all 5,771 Dutch primary schools, weighted ",
      "by number of pupils. Schools are ordered by their average\n",
      "difference across maths and reading. * Classification changes ",
      "depending on how DUO's '<5' counts are handled (tested with\n",
      "1, 2.5 and 4). In this plot '<5' counts are replaced by 2.5. ",
      "Source: DUO."
    )
  ) +
  theme_report

plot_1s_2f
```
